title: Generating Superposition of Transverse Ising Ground States by Quantum Interaction
authors: Koushik Das, Sayan Mondal, Ujjwal Sen
abstract: We investigate superpositions of quantum Ising ground states generated through a quantum interaction, in which the nearest-neighbor coupling strength is promoted to an operator acting on a central auxiliary spin. We prepare the central spin in a superposition, which allows the chain to evolve coherently under different effective interaction strengths. The states are prepared by adiabatic evolution of the joint system comprising the central spin and the many-body spin chain, followed by a measurement on the central spin and post-selection of a specific outcome. It is possible to prepare superpositions of transverse-field quantum Ising ground states belonging to the three magnetic phases, namely, the paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and anti-ferromagnetic phases. For a spin-1/2 central system, it is possible to prepare superpositions of ground states belonging to any two phases, while for the spin-1 case, the superpositions may contain three ground states, each belonging to one of the three phases. We analytically derive expressions for the magnetization, spin correlations, and entanglement of such states. The magnetization and spin correlations show distinct features in different superposition sectors. The nearest-neighbor entanglement is largest where the transverse field and Ising interaction compete, and its behavior differs from that of the magnetic observables. We also derive the quantum Fisher information relevant to estimating the Ising interaction strength. And it exhibits multiple peaks near the critical points of the constituent ground states, with the maximum value showing Heisenberg scaling, for the parameters and system sizes examined.
summary: This paper details a method to generate quantum superpositions of ground states from the transverse-field Ising model by coupling it to a central auxiliary spin. By analyzing observables like magnetization, correlations, and the Quantum Fisher Information, the authors confirm that these superpositions span different magnetic phases. The key finding is the observation of Heisenberg scaling in the QFI, suggesting high sensitivity for parameter estimation near critical points.
main_problem: The study investigates the preparation and characterization of coherent superpositions of ground states of the transverse-field quantum Ising model belonging to different magnetic phases.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrate the preparation of such superpositions and show that the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) exhibits Heisenberg scaling ($L^2$) near critical points.
method: The protocol involves adiabatic evolution of a joint system (Ising chain + central spin) followed by post-selection measurement on the central spin to project the chain into a superposition state.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising chain coupled to a central auxiliary spin (spin-1/2 or spin-1). The Hamiltonian involves nearest-neighbor coupling strength promoted to an operator acting on the central spin.
key_observables: Magnetization, nearest-neighbor spin correlations, entanglement (concurrence), and Quantum Fisher Information (QFI).
important_parameters: Interaction coupling ($J$), transverse field ($h$), and the superposition parameter ($\delta$). The analysis covers the paramagnetic, ferromagnetic, and anti-ferromagnetic phases.
main_assumptions: The state preparation relies on adiabatic evolution, and certain properties are analyzed in the thermodynamic limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept of superpositions across three phases, show the dependence of magnetization and correlations on the $J-\delta$ plane, and display the QFI vs. $J$ plot, confirming $L^2$ scaling.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the model and the state preparation protocol via adiabatic evolution. It then analytically derives expressions for key observables like magnetization and correlations. Finally, it focuses on calculating the QFI, demonstrating its scaling behavior near critical points.
why_interesting: This work connects quantum metrology (QFI scaling) directly to the physics of quantum phase transitions in integrable models, providing a concrete physical realization for quantum sensing based on many-body ground states.
